                     <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jer. 2. 22. Hos. 13. 12.</ns0:note> laid up in store with me, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> sealed up among my treasures?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="35">35 To me <ns0:hi>belongeth</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 12. 19. Heb. 10. 30.</ns0:note> vengeance <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">It is my office to punish sin, and therefore as I know their sins so I will assuredly punish them.</ns0:note> and recom<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pence, their feet shall slide <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">They who now think they stand fast and unmoveable they shall fall into utter destru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ction.</ns0:note> in <ns0:hi>due</ns0:hi> time <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Though not so soon as some may expect it, yet in that time when it shall be most proper and seasonable, when they have filled up the measure of their sins. This <ns0:hi>due time</ns0:hi> may be the same with that <ns0:hi>fulness of time, Gal.</ns0:hi> 4. 4. when Christ came into the world, whom this people by wicked hands crucified and slew, <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 2. 23. for which <ns0:hi>wrath came upon them to the utter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />most,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Thes.</ns0:hi> 2. 15, 16.</ns0:note>: for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Pet. 2. 3.</ns0:note> the day of their calamity <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> at hand <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>is near.</ns0:hi> So the Scripture oft speaks of those things which are at many hundred years distance, to meet with objections arising in mens minds from the delays of them, and to signifie, that though they may be afar off as to our measures of time and expectation of the things, yet in Gods account they are near, they are as near as may be, as soon as ever the fit and the full time is come, they come instantly, they are nearer than sinners would have them, when the measure of their sins is once full, the judgment shall not be deferred.</ns0:note>, and the things that shall come upon them, make haste.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="36">36 For <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Or, <ns0:hi>Nevertheless,</ns0:hi> or, <ns0:hi>But yet,</ns0:hi> as the particle, <ns0:hi>chi,</ns0:hi> is some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />times used, as <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 5. 7. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 9. 1. and 49. 25. Having now spoken of the dreadful calamity which would come upon his people, he now turns his discourse into a more comfortable strain, according to the usual method of the Prophets, and here begins to shew that after God had humbled and sorely chastised his people, yet at last he would have mercy upon them and turn their captivity, as it here follows.</ns0:note> the LORD shall judge his people <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Shall plead their cause, shall protect and deliver them, as that phrase is oft used. See <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 7. 8. and 10. 18. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 1. 17. and 11. 4. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 5. 28. and 22. 16.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 106. 45. Jer. 31. 20.</ns0:note> repent himself for his servants <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Repent of the evils he hath brought upon them, will change his course and carriage towards them.</ns0:note>, when he seeth that <ns0:hi>their</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> hand.</ns0:note> power is gone, and <ns0:hi>there is</ns0:hi> none shut up, or left <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>None shut up,</ns0:hi> either in their strong cities or castles or other hiding places, or in the enemies hands or prisons, whence there might be some hope or possibility of redemption; and none <ns0:hi>left,</ns0:hi> as the poor and contemptible people are neglected and usually left by the conquerours in the conquered land, as 2 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 25. 12. but all seem to be cut off and the people quite destroyed. So this phrase is used 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 14. 10. and 21. 21. and 2 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 9. 8. and 14. 26.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="37">37 And he shall say <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">The Lord, before he deliver his people, will first convince them of their former folly in forsaking him and following Idols: he will find an occasion from that miserable and hopeless con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dition into which their Idols have brought them to upbraid them with it.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Judg. 10. 1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">

                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:note> where <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> their gods, <ns0:hi>their</ns0:hi> rock in whom they trusted?</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="38">38 Which did eat the fat of their sacrifices, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> drank the wine of their drink-offerings <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) To whom you offered sacrifices and oblations after the manner of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles.</ns0:hi> See <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 34. 13. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 106. 28. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 10. 20.</ns0:note>? let them rise up, and help you <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">If they can do it. Compare <ns0:hi>Iudg.</ns0:hi> 10. 14. <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 2. 28.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> be <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">

                        <ns0:hi>for you.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> your protection.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="39">39 See now <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Learn now by your own sad experience what vain and impo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tent things Idols are, and what a silly thing it was in you to put your trust in them, as they did <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 37.</ns0:note>, that <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 102<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">

                     <ns0:hi>there is</ns0:hi> no god with me; <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Sam. 2. 5. Job 5. 18<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Hos. 6. 1.</ns0:note> I kill, and I make alive: I wound, and I heal: neither <ns0:hi>is there any</ns0:hi> that can deliver out of my hand.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="40">40 For I lift up my hand to heaven <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) I solemnly swear, that I will do what here follows, that, as I will deliver my people, so I will fully avenge my self upon all mine enemies, whom I have used as rods to scourge my people.</ns0:note>, and say, I live for ever <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) As sure as I live. Compare <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 4. 2. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 6. 13. <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 10. 5, 6.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

                     </ns0:note> I whet my glittering sword <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">If once I begin to prepare for war and for the execution of my sentence.</ns0:note>, and mine hand take hold on judgment <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) Of the instruments of judgment, of the weapons of war. A metaphor from warriours, that take their weapons into their hand, when they intend to fight.</ns0:note>, I will render vengeance to mine enemies, and will reward them that hate me.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="42">42 I will make mine arrows drunk with blood (and my sword shall devour flesh) <ns0:hi>and that</ns0:hi> with the blood of the slain, and of the captives <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Whom my sword hath sorely wounded, though not utterly killed.</ns0:note>, from the beginning of <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Job 13. 24 Jer. 30. 14 Lam. 2. 5.</ns0:note> revenges upon the enemy <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">(<ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi>) When once I begin to revenge my self and my people upon mine and their enemies, I will go on and make a full end. Or, <ns0:hi>with the head,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>with</ns0:hi> the blood of <ns0:hi>the bead, i. e.</ns0:hi> of the chief or chiefs, <ns0:hi>of the revenges of the enemy, i. e.</ns0:hi> of the re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vengeful or malicious enemy of God and of his people. The noun substantive is oft put for the adjective, as <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 17. 5. <ns0:hi>a multitude of nations</ns0:hi> is put for <ns0:hi>many nations, Rom.</ns0:hi> 4. 17. and <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 45. 22. <ns0:hi>changes of raiment, i. e.</ns0:hi> changeable raiment; and <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 99. 4. <ns0:hi>the kings strength, i. e.</ns0:hi> the strong and mighty king. And so here, <ns0:hi>the revenges of the enemy, i. e.</ns0:hi> the revengeful enemy. And by the <ns0:hi>head</ns0:hi> may be here understood either the Devil, or the heads and rulers of those Empires which were enemies to Gods people. Or, <ns0:hi>of the head</ns0:hi> shall be <ns0:hi>the revenges upon the ene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mies, i. e.</ns0:hi> I will take vengeance upon all mine enemies, yea upon the head or heads of them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="43">43 <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> praise <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> people, ye <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>, or sing ye.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 15. 10.</ns0:note> Rejoyce, O ye nations, <ns0:hi>with</ns0:hi> his peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">This translation is justified by St. <ns0:hi>Paul, Rom.</ns0:hi> 15. 10. the par<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ticle <ns0:hi>with,</ns0:hi> being oft understood, as <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 26. 42. He calls upon the nations to rejoyce and bless God for his favours and especially for the last wonderful deliverance which shall be given to the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> when they shall be converted unto the Gospel in the last days, which they have all reason to do not onely from that duty of sympathy which they owe to all people, and especially to Gods antient people, whereby they are to <ns0:hi>rejoyce with them that rejoyce,</ns0:hi> but because of that singular advantage and happiness which all nations will have at that time and upon that occasion. Or, <ns0:hi>rejoyce, O ye Gentiles, his people, i. e.</ns0:hi> O you Gentiles, who once were not Gods people, but now are his people, do you re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />joyce for Gods mercies to the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> his antient people, bless God for their conversion and salvation.</ns0:note>, for he will avenge the blood of his servants, and will render vengeance to his adversaries, and will be merciful unto his land, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> to his people.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="44">44 And Moses came, and spake all the words of this song in the ears of the people, he, and <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> Ioshua.</ns0:note> Ho<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />shea <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Or <ns0:hi>Ioshua:</ns0:hi> who is here joyned with <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> in this action, because though <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi> onely spake the words, yet <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi> consent<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed to them, and, it may be, afterwards repeated them; this being not a song to be sung once for all, but a standing monu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment which was written and kept for future use, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 31. 22, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> and to be repeated again and again upon solemn occasions, which <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi> and other succeeding Magistrates were to take care of.</ns0:note> the son of Nun.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="45">45 And Moses made an end of speaking all these words to all Israel.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="46">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:169" />46 And he said unto them, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 6. 6. & 11. 18.</ns0:note> Set your hearts unto all the words which I testifie among you this day, which ye shall command your children to ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />serve to do, all the words of this law.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="47">47 For it <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> not a vain thing for you <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">It is not an unprofitable or contemptible work I advise you to, but well worthy of your most serious care oft to remember and diligently to consider it.</ns0:note>, because it is your life, and through this thing ye shall pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />long <ns0:hi>your</ns0:hi> dayes, in the land whither ye go over Jordan to possess it.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="48">48 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Num. 27. 12.</ns0:note> And the LORD spake unto Moses that self-same day, saying,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="49">49 Get thee up into this mountain Abarim, unto mount Nebo <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Nebo</ns0:hi> was a ridge or top of the mountains of <ns0:hi>Abarim.</ns0:hi> See on <ns0:hi>Numb.</ns0:hi> 27. 12. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 3. 27.</ns0:note>, which <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> in the land of Moab, that <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> over against Jericho, and behold the land of Canaan, which I give unto the children of Is<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rael for a possession:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="50">50 And die in the mount whither thou goest up, and be gathered unto thy people, as <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Num. 20. 25, 28. & 33. 38.</ns0:note> Aaron thy brother died in mount Hor, and was gathered un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to his people.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="51">51 Because <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Num. 20. 12, 13. & 27. 14.</ns0:note> ye trespassed against me, among the children of Israel, at the waters of <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> strife at Kadesh.</ns0:note> Meribah<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />kadesh in the wilderness of Zin: because ye san<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctified me not in the midst of the children of Israel.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="52">52 Yet thou shalt see the land before <ns0:hi>thee,</ns0:hi> but thou shalt not go thither unto the land which I give the children of Israel.</ns0:p>
